newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says no deal on late Italy EMU entry.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says no deal on late Italy EMU entry.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday he knew of no deal to postpone Italy's entry into European monetary union, and said Rome's joining depended on fulfilling the Maastricht treaty convergence criteria.

Waigel also said he was happy about the U.S. dollar's gains against the German mark: "A year ago we had a weak dollar and everyone was wondering what to do about it. No we have a strong dollar and we should be satisfied," he told reporters.

Commenting on a report in Wednesday's Financial Times that senior European monetary officials and central bankers had offered a deal to delay Italy's entry into EMU beyond the planned 1999 start date, Waigel said he knew of no such plan.
"I know of no such considerations," Waigel said.
And, asked if Italy would be part of the first round of EMU participants, he said: "That depends on the criteria."
The Maastricht treaty sets a budget deficit limit of three percent of gross domestic product which must be met this year if countries are to join the single currency's launch in 1999.

Italian leaders angrily rejected suggestions that Rome put off joining, with Prime Minister Romano Prodi -- who visits Germany on Friday -- declaring himself "solemnly committed" to joining the first wave of EMU states.
